author: Antonialock
body:
I had a user request assigned to me to update GO annotation for PCSK1N (ProSAAS) to cover its "important chaperone activity". I've looked at a few papers but I'm not sure what terms to select

From mainly in vitro studies I made the following statements:
"May act as a protein chaperone that prevents the aggregation of client proteins and plays a role in neuroprotection"
"May prevent aggregation of amyloid beta, IAPP/islet amyloid polypeptide, and SNCA/alpha-synuclein" (e.g. 35527562, 24102330)

In vivo, it has been shown to "Block the trans-synaptic spread of SNCA/alpha-synuclein in the brain"

I one study, the authors forced cytoplasmic expression (it normally localizes to the TGN and is secreted, it may function at both locations), and from that paper I got the description
"May form spheres that encapsulate client proteins" (35549000)

Also, it "Cannot disaggregate preformed fibrils" (27457957) or refold unfolded proteins

So it is presumably  a chaperone that prevents aggregation of aggregate-prone proteins, but it doesn't have disaggregase activity or protein folding activity, and I presume unfolded protein holdase activity is also not correct....?

@ValWood @pgaudet
title: term suitable to describe PCSK1N (ProSAAS)

author: ValWood
body: @hattrill  and I came across exactly this combination last week. @hattrill  which protein was it?

author: Antonialock
body: I've also seen protein 7b2/SCG5 mentioned, could it be that one?

author: ValWood
body: I think it was zim17 (human DNLZ). We ended up not adding an MF for now but this seems to be the term we would need. Prevents aggregation of  folded proteins.

author: ValWood
body:
helens notes:
“Zim17/DNLZ maintains mtHsp70/Ssc "structural integrity" - basically seems to stop the chaperone aggregating. I annotated the human protein as "protein folding chaperone" but this is not right. It's not a holdase, protein folding chaperone or a carrier. It's described as a chaperone for chaperones or a co-chaperone.
The IBA is protein-folding chaperone binding - do you think that this is the best we can do for an MF?” Used “Hsp70 protein binding” until we have a better term to describe proteins that prevent the aggregation of folded proteins.

author: hattrill
body:
Yep - CG12379 in flies ; Human DNLZ ; UniProtKB:Q5SXM8
So, yes, acts on folded proteins that are prone to aggregating to stop them aggregating. Often called co-chaperones, but this terms is used for a multitude of functions. 

I feed this to claude and they said "protein aggregation inhibitor activity" with this def:
"Prevents the self-association and aggregation of folded or natively-structured proteins without refolding unfolded substrates or disaggregating pre-formed fibrillar assemblies. Acts on client proteins that are in a folded or partially-folded aggregation-competent state." 
with Suggested synonyms

anti-aggregation chaperone activity (exact)
protein aggregation prevention activity (exact)
protein aggregation suppressor activity (related)

Not sure if I love it and not sure where it would sit, but it's a seed.

author: pgaudet
body: Did the user tell you which papers demonstrated its "important chaperone activity" ? The evidence don't seem super strong, unless we can be pointed to reliable papers.

author: Antonialock
body:
I think the best evidence is for  SNCA/alpha-synuclein -
In my understanding:
- alpha-synuclein is predominantly cytosolic and found at synapses, but some proportion is secreted (https://journals.plos.org/plosone/article?id=10.1371/journal.pone.0022225)
- It is a major component of parkinson's Lewy body inclusions
- I think Parkinsons spreads throughout the brain as the disease progresses, and this protein has been suggested to prevent this spread - some kind of detoxification?

"Our finding of substoichiometric blockade of α-synuclein fibrillation, coupled with the demonstration of immunoreactive proSAAS within Lewy bodies, indicates that proSAAS could function upstream of cytotoxic processes by i**nteracting with intracellular α-synuclein monomers in a transition state** ([68](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4987805/#r68)) **that would otherwise propagate toward toxic fibril formation, or by interacting with oligomers to prevent further oligomerization, fibrillation, and cytotoxicity**. However, as mentioned above, addition of extracellular proSAAS was ineffective in blocking intracellular α-synuclein oligomerization, although still attenuating cytotoxicity. We speculate that proSAAS may bind only to secreted forms of α-synuclein or bind to already-formed intracellular α-synuclein oligomers, reducing further growth. Alternatively, proSAAS might prevent the seeding of additional oligomers, perhaps through blocking of hydrophobic patches necessary for fibril formation. Once bound, proSAAS may blunt the toxic actions of α-synuclein in much the same way that antibody fragments against α-synuclein are able to prevent cytotoxicity" https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4987805/

author: pgaudet
body:
Thanks. I think that corresponds to [protein-containing complex destabilizing activity](http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_0140776) ? 

A molecular function that involves direct binding to one of the subunits of a protein-containing complex and promoting the dissociation of one or many subunits. This often happens by changing the conformation of the protein being bound, which decreases its affinity for the rest of the complex.

author: Antonialock
body: Yes thanks that could work - is it ok for when the "complex" is a toxic aggregate?

author: pgaudet
body: I think so ? This is is a function, it should be agnostic WRT to process (again some sort of detoxification or damage removal)

author: Antonialock
body: ok, I have annotated to that term + detoxification. Thanks for the advise all.
